scope: Public official documentation only; no CLI/API execution, provider calls, local configuration, or secrets accessed.

evidence_grades.A: Official vendor documentation page, retrieved on the research date.
evidence_grades.B: Official project documentation from mutable GitHub main/master, retrieved on the research date; version is not pinned.

roles.agent_client: A human-facing client consumes MCP tools and may run its own agent loop.
roles.agent_runner: A runtime starts agent turns, owns tools and sessions, and reports lifecycle state.
roles.model_inference_endpoint: A model-only API/proxy forwards inference; it does not necessarily expose an agent session or MCP tools.
roles.distinction: OpenCode and Hermes have client and runner surfaces. Hermes separately documents an agent API server and a model-only subscription proxy. MCPO exposes MCP tools as OpenAPI/REST and is not an inference gateway. MCPO use_loopback is a local OAuth callback option, not an inference product.

model_inventory.notes: CLI lists models from configured providers; verbose output includes model metadata such as cost. HTTP inventory returns provider/default-model or connected-provider metadata. No read-secret endpoint established; PUT /auth/:id is a credential-write route.

execution.permission_response: POST /session/{id}/permissions/{permissionID}; agent/tool permission response, not provider-native approval.
execution.server_auth: OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD enables HTTP Basic authentication; username may be configured with OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME.

mcp.notes: Local stdio and remote HTTP MCP servers are configured in OpenCode config. Remote OAuth can use discovery/DCR and stores client credentials locally; do not copy its auth file.

auth_billing_usage.notes: opencode auth login/list/logout manages local provider auth; baseURL is configurable. Docs list specific subscription integrations (including ChatGPT Plus and GitHub Copilot), while explicitly saying Anthropic prohibits former Claude Pro/Max plugin use and that plugin is no longer bundled since 1.3.0. opencode stats reports session token/cost statistics. No universal provider-quota API documented.

headless.notes: -z is a scripted one-shot with machine-distinguishable exit codes and optional --usage-file JSON. serve is a headless JSON-RPC/WebSocket backend, separate from the OpenAI-compatible API server.

agent_api.auth: API_SERVER_KEY bearer token required; docs warn the server exposes the full agent toolset including terminal commands. Multi-profile routes use profile-specific keys.
agent_api.notes: Run status exposes lifecycle state, usage and requested/actual runtime provider-model. Stop is cooperative and remains tracked until executor exit. Approval and clarify bind to the current pending control identity/generation. /v1/models is only the agent alias; /api/model/options is the richer provider/model catalog. refresh=1 probes custom provider endpoints; do not use for passive inventory.

mcp.notes: Hermes consumes local stdio and remote HTTP MCP servers, and docs also list running Hermes as an MCP server. hermes import-agent can copy MCP configuration but explicitly does not import provider keys/credentials.

auth_subscription_usage.notes: hermes auth manages provider credentials/OAuth, but technical login is not a general provider subscription permission. Nous Portal is an explicit subscription. hermes proxy is model-only inference for documented OAuth upstreams, not an agent runner; its client bearer is replaced by the stored upstream credential. hermes usage --json documents account windows for OpenAI Codex, Anthropic OAuth, and OpenRouter. -z --usage-file reports estimated cost/tokens/API calls and auxiliary work; not a hard budget guarantee.

management.prerequisite: STORE_MODEL_IN_DB enabled for API model creation/update/deletion.
management.auth: Official add example uses LITELLM_MASTER_KEY; delete is documented admin-only. GET /model/info masks API keys.
management.notes: config.yaml models remain file-owned and cannot be managed/deleted through the database API/UI; choose a single source of truth.

health.notes: Liveness/readiness check process/dependencies. /health sends real test requests to configured models, costs a few tokens per model, and accepts any valid key; it is active inference, not passive health metadata. Authenticated details can reveal URLs/errors.

mcpo.notes: Wraps stdio or supported HTTP MCP transport and exposes OpenAPI/REST tool handlers and /docs. OAuth can use DCR. use_loopback defaults true for local browser OAuth callback (callback_port defaults 3030); it does not denote model inference or an inference gateway.

unknowns: No universal OpenCode provider quota endpoint or provider-native approval API was established in the reviewed docs.
Provider subscription permission and API-vs-consumer terms remain specific to each vendor; OAuth support alone is not evidence of entitlement.
Installed versions, user profiles, actual provider health, quota, and real costs were not inspected or executed.
Hermes custom-provider refresh performs endpoint probes; exact model visibility depends on the selected provider, profile, cache, and runtime version.
minimum_viable_integration: Treat agent launch, model inference, and MCP tool access as separate adapters and permissions.
Use explicit local profile registration and documented non-secret metadata; never scrape credential files or accept executable/session/provider choices from event input.
Make new runs, stop, agent permission approvals, provider OAuth, and model refresh explicit operator actions; track unknown usage/quota as unknown.
Protect headless APIs as privileged control planes, especially Hermes API_SERVER_KEY and OpenCode server credentials.
